newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks in surprise rally close up 4.51 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks in surprise rally close up 4.51 pct.

text.p: Thai stocks roared to a surprisingly strong close on Wednesday in a busy afternoonm session on broad buying by local retail and foreign investors, brokers said.
The SET Index rose 31.59 points, or 4.51 percent, to close at 731.74. The SET 50 finished 3.20 points up at 54.07.

"The announcement by the Bank of Thailand yesterday saying that there would be no change to the baht was the main factor on the market," said an analyst at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities. Others said a technical rebound was behind the gains and noted that a weakening dollar had helped overall.
The Bank of Thailand issued a statement on Tuesday dismissing market speculation of a voluntary baht devaluation.
Sentiment in the battered market was also boosted by a weaker dollar which increased baht liquidity in the Thai money market on Wednesday, traders said.
The Wednesday rally of the SET Index was its largest single day gain since former Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa dissolved parliament on September 30 last year.
Bargain hunters, encouraged by higher liquidity and lower interbank lending rates, focused on deeply discounted finance stocks which advanced 7.69 percent.
Retail investors see downside risk limited by local mutual funds operating a support scheme which recently succeeded in keeping the market above 700, traders said.

Prospects for more gains on Thursday are heightened by Wednesday's moderate 5.82 billion baht turnover. "I think there is a chance for the rally to continue tomorrow since volume is quite high today," he said, adding that selective foreign buying emerged in commmunications, bank and energy stocks.
Bangkok Bank gained seven baht to 171, UCOM added eight to 161, Advanced Info put on 22 to 242, and EGCO rose 3.50 to 62.50. -- James Mclean (662) 652-0642
